title: Ralph Wiggum: Continuous Agent Loops in Claude Code
summary: AI Makerspace explains the Ralph Wiggum loop plugin (stop-hook re-prompting) and argues it suits low-stakes, verifiable work, not your job.

assertions.quote: when Claude tries to stop, we say, No, no, no. It's not time to stop

verdicts.note: Goal/loop features keep agents going through backlogs, but unattended runs drift or game checks without good verification; works when acceptance tests are strong.

assertions.quote: It's not good for tasks requiring human judgment ... don't use Ralph at work

verdicts.note: Loops without human checkpoints work when tests define success; for ambiguous or high-stakes work, drift, false completion and token burn dominate. Matches vendor guidance on long-running harnesses.

Anthropic: engineers fully delegate easily verifiable, low-stakes work (throwaway debug or research code) and keep supervising high-stakes work; this is about delegation in general, not unattended loops specifically.

assertions.quote: if I want Claude to work for for 10 hours on something, I best have put 10 hours into planning

verdicts.note: Clear requirements, examples and references reliably improve agent output; the caveat is that bloated context can hurt, so curation matters.

assertions.quote: tasks with automatic verification ... if we make it superverifiable

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: Every time I do something more than once with Claude, I turn it into a skill

verdicts.note: Reusable commands/skills reduce variance and share practice across a team; the 'three times' threshold is a rule of thumb.

assertions.quote: if I notice Claude has made a mistake ... I'm simply going to tell Claude to remember to not make that mistake

verdicts.note: Encoding lessons in rules and workflows does reduce repeat mistakes, but rule files bloat and conflict if not pruned; gains are real but not automatically compounding.
Airbnb's 'sample, tune, sweep' loop (find common failures, fix the prompt/scripts, re-run) raised completion from 75% to 97% in 4 days.

assertions.quote: dangerously run permissions mode which uh which you should never do unless you're in a sandbox

verdicts.note: Agents have deleted files and run destructive commands when unrestricted; vendors themselves recommend containers/VMs for skip-permissions modes.
Sandboxing appears in 15% (5/33) of safeguard sources (e.g. Seatbelt read-only jail, Docker plus iptables isolation) and is a recommended practice, but its effectiveness is not evaluated.
